newsitem.title: USA: US rates safety of 5 foreign aviation authorities.
newsitem.headline: US rates safety of 5 foreign aviation authorities.

text.p: U.S. officials on Tuesday said that Saudi Arabia and Singapore met international safety oversight standards for their airlines, but Pakistan and Nauru were rated conditional and Malta unacceptable.

The Federal Aviation Administration said the ratings did not indicate whether an individual foreign airline was safe, but whether a national aviation authority was in place and whether it ensured the safe operations of its airlines.

It said the assessments were based on the safety standards of the International Civil Aviation Organization. Under U.S. law, countries whose airlines fly into the United States must abide by the ICAO standards.

Pakistan and the Pacific Ocean island nation of Nauru were rated conditional because of some safety shortcomings, the FAA said. It added that the lapses were being corrected and meanwhile flights to America were allowed under heightened FAA oversight.
Because Malta was listed as unacceptable, flights to the United States would not be allowed unless they were flown by an airline certified by a country meeting ICAO safety standards, the FAA said.
The United States is in the process of rating the aviation authorities of all countries whose airlines fly into the United States or who ask that their authorities be assessed.
